messages:
pagerduty: URGENT: High error rate and increased latency observed for model family aurora-9b across us-west-2. Incident ID PD-4521. Paging eng-sre oncall.

oncall-bot: auto-signal: anomaly detected: aurora-9b TPM spike + 1200% over baseline, 15m window. Routing to eng-sre channel.

alex: saw the spike, a handful of heavy streaming customers + function_calling enabled. 5000 TPM for aurora-9b right now.

maya: confirmed elevated 5xxs from gateway logs ~09:02 UTC, tail latency > 2.5s. Customers A and B reporting timeouts.

samir: quick ask — can we soft-limit TPM for aurora-9b to stop token storm? Propose drop to 900 TPM for emergency window.

jasper: +1 to rapid TPM cap. We should also turn off function-calling for that family temporarily (some customers spike due to open loops).

alex: executing mitigation now. CLI to run:```sh
redwoodctl quota set --model aurora-9b --tpm 900 --rpm 12000 --reason "emergency sculpt - live mitigation"
redwoodctl feature toggle --model aurora-9b --feature function_calling --state off --reason "reduce storm"
```

alex: ran both commands, control plane acknowledged. roll-id: roll-aurora-3723.

oncall-bot: action-log: quota:update roll-aurora-3723 by alex at 09:06 UTC. feature: function_calling disabled for aurora-9b.

maya: monitoring metrics — request rate dropped ~78% within 30s, error-rate falling. Latency decreasing toward baseline.

samir: pinging support to let customers A/B know we're mitigating and to collect any in-flight requests.

jasper: note — we saw a pattern: customers with long-running function loops hit KV cache misses which amplified token churn. Keep an eye on cache hit ratio.

alex: cache-hit-rate for aurora-9b jumped down pre-mitigation. Kicked a small cache-warm job targeting top prefixes.

maya: customer impact update: Customer A saw ~12% failed requests during spike window, B had ephemeral latency spikes but recoveries after cap. No data plane breaches.

samir: ops question — do we also want to gate by customer tier? maybe set a per-customer rate carve for free tier first.

jasper: yes but that is heavier lift mid-incident. For now keep family-level cap, note action item for postmortem to implement priority-based throttles.

alex: putting a temporary note in the incident ticket: PD-4521 — temp measures: aurora-9b TPM 900, function_calling disabled. Owner: alex.

oncall-bot: paging reminder: escalation to SRE Lead in 20m if degraded metrics persist.

maya: metrics stable for 6m, error-rate trending to baseline. Recommend hold mitigation for 30m, then gradual lift to 2500 TPM while observing.

samir: agree. I'll prepare a small canary plan: lift to 1500 TPM first for 10m, then 2500 if stable.

jasper: make sure to annotate release/rollout and link impacted customers in the ticket. Also capture logs for KV cache regression.

alex: starting canary now:```sh
redwoodctl quota set --model aurora-9b --tpm 1500 --reason "canary lift PD-4521"
```

oncall-bot: action-log: quota:update roll-aurora-3723-canary by alex at 09:24 UTC.

maya: canary looks OK so far (3m). No spike in 5xx, latency ~1.1s.

samir: hold and watch 10m then proceed to 2500 if steady. I'm drafting customer comms for affected customers.

jasper: also add a follow-up ticket to add automated per-customer throttles and function_calling heuristics. Tagging eng-runtime and eng-oncall.

alex: noted. I'll hand off to night oncall at 09:50 UTC. current status: aurora-9b TPM 1500, function_calling still disabled, metrics stable.

maya: thanks — great quick work team. Closing the immediate mitigation when we reach the 30m watch window and update PD ticket with timeline. :thumbsup:

samir: moving to post-incident doc after closure. Will include root-cause hypothesis: function-calling loops + cache misses -> token storm.

pagerduty: Incident PD-4521 status: mitigated -> monitoring. Assigned: alex. Next update due in 60m.
